senses.def: to dedicate to the service of and to loyalty to deity
senses.comment: Though in certain contexts ἁγιάζω[a] and ἁγιασμός suggest resulting moral behavior, the emphasis is not upon a manner of life but upon religious activity and observances which reflect one’s dedication or consecration to God. Accordingly, in 1 Corinthians 1:2 one may translate ἁγιάζω as who have given themselves to God or who serve God with a whole heart.

senses.domain: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior
senses.def: to cause someone to have the quality of holiness

senses.domain: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior
senses.def: to feel reverence for or to honor as holy
senses.comment: In a number of languages it is impossible to employ an expression such as ‘your name’ as a reference for God himself. Therefore, it may be necessary to translate this expression in Matthew 6:9 as ‘may you be reverenced as holy’ or even ‘may you be acknowledged as God.’

senses.def: pertaining to not being able to do or experience something
senses.comment: In Romans 15:1 οἱ δυνατοί refers to capability with respect to faith and τῶν ἀδυνάτων refers, conversely, to those who are incapable with respect to faith. In some languages, therefore, it may be possible to use a similar biblical phrase, weak in the faith.|In many languages the appropriate equivalent of Acts 14:8 would be but in Lystra there was a man who was crippled.

senses.def: pertaining to being impossible, presumably because of a lack of power to alter or control circumstances
senses.comment: In Hebrews 6:4 the use of ἀδύνατον seems to be an instance of hyperbole in view of the warnings against apostasy (see Hebrews 5:11). Therefore, one may translate ἀδύνατον in Hebrews 6:4 as ‘it is extremely difficult to.’ TEV introduces a rhetorical question to express strong doubt, “for how can those who abandon their faith be brought back to repent again?”

senses.domain: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior
senses.def: the state of moral impurity, especially in relationship to sexual sin
any substance which is filthy or dirty
a marker of more emphatic contrast (as compared with δέ[c], 89.124)
senses.comment: ἀλλά also occurs with μᾶλλον and ἤ in more emphatic phrases marking contrast: ἀλλὰ μᾶλλον δουλευέτωσαν ‘on the contrary, they are to serve (them) even better’ 1 Timothy 6:2; οὐχί, λέγω ὑμῖν, ἀλλ᾽ ἢ διαμερισμόν ‘not (peace), I tell you, but rather division’ Luke 12:51.

senses.def: a marker of a series of coordinate relations which are contrastive with a previously identified event or state
a marker of transition, with a slightly adversative implication in some contexts, often best left untranslated
senses.comment: In Romans 15:21 there is certainly no adversative value in the conjunction ἀλλά; if anything, it would only mark some underlying reason, but again it seems best to leave ἀλλά untranslated and to regard it simply as a transitional marker.

senses.def: a marker of contrastive emphasis
a marker of sets of items in contrast with one another
glosses: on the one hand … but on the other hand

senses.def: to put on clothes, implying the clothing being completely around; see also 49.5
to put on clothing to adorn the outward form of something
to think or reason with thoroughness and completeness
pertaining to being impossible to understand on the basis of careful examination or investigation
to answer insults or slander with insulting or slanderous words
pertaining to the lack of knowledge or capacity to do something
to receive, with probable focus upon the source
to receive back something which one has previously possessed or its equivalent
to lead or take away from a particular point
to accept the presence of a person with friendliness
to experience some event or state, often with the implication of something negatively valued
the content of what is expressed in a curse
senses.comment: It may be difficult or even meaningless to speak of a person’s mouth as being ‘full of bitter curses,’ but one can often say ‘they are constantly cursing harshly’ or ‘… speaking heavy curses’ or ‘… constantly uttering harmful curses.’

senses.def: initiation of an action, process, or state of being
senses.comment: It would also be possible to treat ἀρχή in Mark 1:1 as indicating sequence (Domain 61), so that the contents of verse 1 could be regarded as a type of title for the following section. It seems far better, however, to regard ἀρχή in Mark 1:1 as being closely related to what immediately follows in verse 2, so that one may translate ‘the good news about Jesus Christ the Son of God began as the prophet Isaiah had written …’

senses.subdomain: A Point of Time with Reference to Duration of Time: Beginning, End
senses.def: a point of time at the beginning of a duration
one who or that which constitutes an initial cause
senses.comment: It is also possible to understand ἀρχή in Revelation 3:14 as meaning ‘ruler’ (see 37.56).

senses.def: the sphere of one’s authority or rule
(derivative of ἄρχω ‘to rule,’ 37.54) one who rules or governs
(title for supernatural forces and powers) a supernatural power having some particular role in controlling the destiny and activities of human beings
senses.comment: Some scholars have believed that it is possible to reconstruct at least in part some of the hierarchy represented by these various supernatural forces and powers, on the basis of the neoplatonic system of nine such powers arranged in three orders of three each. NT terminology and usage does not, however, lend itself to such a classification, and it is difficult, if not impossible, to determine what are the significant differences between these supernatural powers and forces.|In the case of Ephesians 1:21 some scholars apply the terms in question both to the supernatural and to the human sphere, thus emphasizing the totality of Christ’s rule. This has a considerable measure of justification in view of the concepts held by persons in the ancient world, since various earthly powers were supposed to reflect corresponding supernatural powers.|For the most part, translators have endeavored to render the various terms in somewhat different ways, for example, ἐξουσία as ‘authority’; δύναμις as ‘power’; κυριότης as ‘ruler’; and phrases such as τὰ πνευματικὰ τῆς πονηρίας ἐν τοῖς ἐπουρανίοις as ‘wicked spiritual forces in the heavenly world.’ In a number of languages, however, there are simply not enough terms to designate various kinds of powers, authorities, and forces which could be employed in speaking of such supernatural impersonal powers. Accordingly, some translators have simply used a phrase such as ‘any and all kinds of supernatural powers.’ Where it is possible to make certain lexical distinctions between terms and phrases, this, of course, should be done, but in a number of contexts this may be impossible, and accordingly, some explanation in a marginal note may be required if the reader is to understand satisfactorily the intent of the passages in question.|In some instances a measure of meaning may be obtained by somewhat paraphrastic expressions. For example, Ephesians 2:2 is rendered in some languages as ‘at that time you lived in the way in which the spirit that governs this world dictated you should live. This is the way the one who rules over the power in space commanded you to live. This is the very spirit that now commands the people who disobey God.’

senses.subdomain: Basic Principles or Features Defining the Nature of Something
senses.def: elementary and preliminary aspects defining the nature of something
senses.comment: Compare also the occurrence of ἀρχή[g] in Hebrews 5:12 in which it serves to reinforce the meaning of στοιχεῖα (see 58.19).

senses.def: the corner of a two-dimensional object, such as a sheet of cloth
pertaining to being unattractive or unseemly
to keep thinking about, without having one’s attention distracted
to acquire information, with focus presumably upon the source of such information
pertaining to a king
senses.comment: The expression ‘his royal robes’ may be rendered as ‘his clothing which he had as king,’ and the phrase ‘the royal priesthood’ may be rendered as ‘priests who are like kings.’

senses.def: an official directly responsible to a king
(derivative of βλέπω[a] ‘to see,’ 24.7) that which is seen or that which one becomes aware of
a district in the Roman province of Asia
(derivative of γογγύζω ‘to complain,’ 33.382) one who has a habit of complaining or grumbling
a set of beliefs concerning deity, with the implication of corresponding behavior
one who succeeds another in a position or responsibility
to remain or stay in a place, with the implication of some type of activity
an indefinitely large number (even greater than μυριάς[b], 60.8)
senses.comment: Though it is possible to understand δισμυριάδες μυριάδων in Revelation 9:16 as meaning ‘two hundred million’ (literally ‘twenty thousand times ten thousand’), the evident intent of the text is to emphasize the extreme number rather than to specify some large quantity.

senses.def: to attribute ill repute or bad reputation to
a pattern of behavior more or less fixed by tradition and generally sanctioned by the society
senses.comment: In a number of languages there is no noun for ‘custom’ or ‘habit,’ but the same meaning is communicated by verbal aspects or adverbial phrases indicating habitual action. For example, in the case of John 19:40 one may translate in some languages ‘as is the way in which Jews always bury people,’ and for 1 Corinthians 11:16 one may translate ‘this is not what we constantly do.’

senses.def: a position relatively far from the speaker, writer, or viewpoint person
to provide food for, with the implication of a considerable period of time and the food being adequate nourishment
glosses: to give food to someone to eat

senses.def: to raise a child to maturity by providing for physical and psychological needs
senses.comment: To raise or bring up children may be expressed in a number of different ways, for example, ‘to give food to children,’ ‘to take care of children,’ ‘to be a parent to children,’ ‘to cause a child to become an adult,’ or ‘to make a child become like oneself.’

senses.def: The meaning of ἐμβατεύω, which occurs only once in the NT, namely, in Colossians 2:18, is obscure. It may mean more or less literally ‘to set foot upon’ or ‘to enter’ or possibly ‘to come into possession of.’ It may also mean ‘to enter into’ in the sense of to go into detail in treating a subject, but it seems more likely that ἐμβατεύω in Colossians 2:18 is a technical term derived from the mystery religions, and it could be interpreted in the phrase ἅ ἑόρακεν ἐμβατεύων as meaning ‘who enters the sanctuary which he saw in ecstasy’ or ‘taking his stand on what he has seen in the mysteries.’ In view of the context, which speaks of someone being puffed up without cause, one might also render this Greek phrase as ‘by what he saw when he was initiated.’ For further data on this semantically difficult term, see A Greek-English Lexicon of the New Testament, University of Chicago Press, third edition edited by Danker (BDAG).
a marker of cause or reason, often with the implication of purpose in the sense of ‘for the sake of’
a marker of purpose, with the frequent implication of some underlying reason
(with the genitive) a marker of a participant constituting the reason for an event
senses.comment: In Acts 28:20 there is an ellipsis of a reference to the person who is the object of the hope.

senses.def: to come back to life after having once died
senses.comment: In a number of languages there is a difficulty involved in formulating some expression for ‘resurrection’ or ‘living again,’ since such a phrase may refer to what is technically known as metempsychosis, that is to say, the rebirth of the soul in another existence, a belief which is widely held in a number of areas of south Asia. This problem may be avoided in some languages by speaking of ‘his body will live again’ or ‘his body will come back to life’ or ‘he will be the same person when he lives again.’|The phrase ‘the resurrection from among the dead’ may be rendered as ‘to live again’ or ‘to live again after having died.’

senses.def: to cause to recall and to think about again
glosses: to cause to think about again

senses.def: that which causes something to be known as or to appear to be other than it really is, thus causing its true nature to be unknown
glosses: means of covering up the true nature of something

senses.def: (derivative of ἐπιτάσσω ‘to order, to instruct,’ 33.325) that which has been specifically ordered or commanded
the right or authority to command
senses.comment: It is also possible to translate this expression in Titus 2:15 as ‘show that you have every right to command when you rebuke them.’

senses.subdomain: Definite Units of Time: Year, Month, Week, Day, Hour
senses.def: a period from late in the afternoon until darkness
devoted service to God
a collective of two
a state of undisturbed quietness and calm
senses.comment: ‘To earn their own living’ (2 Thessalonians 3:12) is a rendering of an idiom which is literally ‘to eat their own bread’ (see 57.190). For an interpretation of ἡσυχία in 2 Thessalonians 3:12 focusing on personal behavior, see 88.103.

senses.def: act of maintaining a state of silence, with a possible focus upon the attitude involved

senses.def: act of living in a quiet, peaceful, mild manner
senses.comment: For another interpretation of ἡσυχία in 2 Thessalonians 3:12, focusing on the circumstances involved, see 22.43.

senses.def: the activity of a baby feeding at the breast
senses.comment: In a number of languages there are highly specific terms for the manner in which babies nurse, including ‘to suck upon’ or ‘to pull at the breasts.’ There may also be distinctions in terminology depending upon whether the child in question is a helpless infant held in the arms or a small child capable of moving about. See also discussion at 23.8.

senses.def: to cause a baby to feed at the breast
senses.comment: In many languages entirely distinct terms are employed for the causative and noncausative meanings of ‘to nurse.’ Still additional distinctions may be employed depending upon the age of the child. One term may be used in speaking of helpless infants, while another may be used of small children who are able to walk around, but who still are nursed from time to time.

senses.domain: Body, Body Parts, and Body Products
senses.def: the watery fluid excreted through the pores of the skin

to arm completely with weapons
senses.comment: In some languages the equivalent of ‘to be fully armed’ is ‘to have all the weapons one needs to defend oneself’ or ‘to have the weapons needed in order to be safe.’

senses.def: to continue to persist in any undertaking or state
to destroy completely, with the possible implication of something being used up or consumed
to devour something completely

senses.def: (a figurative extension of meaning of κατεσθίω[a] ‘to eat up,’ 23.11) to destroy completely (in a sense more emphatic than ἐσθίω[b], 20.44)
(a figurative extension of meaning of κατεσθίω[a] ‘to eat up, to consume,’ 23.11) to take over by dishonest means the property of someone else
(a figurative extension of meaning of κατεσθίω[a] ‘to eat up, to consume,’ 23.11) to spend or use up excessively and uselessly

senses.domain: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior

to put something over or around the mouths of animals so as to prevent them from eating
senses.comment: In some languages it may be necessary to employ some type of descriptive equivalent of ‘to muzzle,’ for example, ‘do not tie the mouth of the ox so that it cannot eat’ or ‘do not cover the mouth of the ox so that it cannot eat.’

senses.def: pertaining to sharing with someone else in a possession or a relationship implying mutual interest
senses.comment: Since the emphasis in Titus 1:4 is upon the fact that Paul and Titus have the same faith, one may also translate as ‘… the faith that you and I have’ or ‘… the faith we both believe in.’

senses.def: pertaining to being ritually unacceptable, either as the result of defilement or because of the very nature of the object itself (for example, ritually unacceptable animals)
senses.comment: It is possible that there is some subtle distinction in meaning, particularly on a connotative level, between κοινός[b] and ἀκάθαρτος in Acts 10:14, but it is difficult to determine the precise differences of meaning on the basis of existing contexts. The two terms are probably used in Acts 10:14 primarily for the sake of emphasis.

senses.def: pertaining to being of little value, in view of being ordinary and common
pertaining to being in common between two or more persons
senses.comment: It is also possible to understand κοινός in Jude 1:3 as κοινός[a] ‘shared, mutual’ (see 57.9).

senses.def: to hold on to an object
to exercise power or force over someone or something
senses.comment: See discussion at 37.17.

senses.def: to take a person into custody for alleged illegal activity
to cause a state to continue, on the basis of some authority or power
senses.comment: In this expression in John 20:23 it is the state of being guilty of sin which is caused to continue. See also discussion at 40.8.

senses.def: to be able to complete or finish, presumably despite difficulties

relatively small light brown domestic animal, feeding on anything from household refuse to animal carcasses and excreta; Canis familiaris putiatini; associated with all sorts of uncleanness, aggression, greediness, low status
senses.comment: In Greek outside the NT κύων may be either masculine or feminine and in the plural may refer to both male and female dogs.

senses.domain: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior
senses.def: (a figurative extension of meaning of κύων[a] ‘dog,’ 4.34) a particularly bad person, perhaps specifically one who ridicules what is holy
senses.comment: It is also possible that κύων in Philippians 3:2 may be interpreted as meaning ‘pervert’ (see 88.282).|A term for ‘dog’ may have quite a different connotation than it does in English. For example, to call a person ‘a dog’ in some languages is to compliment him for his faithfulness, but in other languages it may be merely a way of attributing promiscuous sexual behavior.

senses.domain: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior
senses.def: (a figurative extension of meaning of κύων[a] ‘dog,’ 4.34) one who is a sexual pervert or possibly one who is sexually promiscuous
senses.comment: It is also possible, however, that in Revelation 22:15 κύων means ‘a wicked person’ who might have complete contempt for what is holy, a meaning which parallels the significance of the adage in Matthew 7:6 (see 88.122).

senses.def: an instrument for pressing out the juice of grapes for the making of wine
senses.comment: Ancient wine presses consisted of large vats into which grapes were placed and then trampled on in order to extract the juice. Accordingly, a descriptive equivalent of wine press may be ‘a place where the juice of grapes was squeezed out’ or ‘… pressed out.’

senses.def: a person in the genealogy of Jesus

senses.domain: Body, Body Parts, and Body Products
senses.def: the breast of both humans and animals, with special reference to the mammary glands
senses.comment: In Revelation 1:13 the phrase πρὸς τοῖς μαστοῖς is a reference to the particular location of the gold band which went around the chest and not to the mammary glands as such. In some languages, therefore, it is often preferable to use a phrase such as ‘around his chest’ rather than trying to be more specific, for example, ‘a gold band around his chest at the location of his breasts.’|In translating Luke 11:27 it is important to use an expression which will be perfectly natural, for example, ‘the breasts that gave you milk’ or ‘the breasts from which you obtained milk.’ In some instances, however, a specific reference to breasts as the source of milk may seem somewhat vulgar, and therefore it may be better to speak of ‘happy is your mother who nursed you.’

senses.def: a state of being tainted or stained by evil
cardinal number, where there are ten thousand instances of a countable entity
pertaining to what is extremely numerous
senses.comment: It would be possible to interpret μυρίους in 1 Corinthians 4:15 as meaning literally ‘ten thousand’ (see 60.45), but the evident intent in this context is to emphasize the indefinitely large number rather than any specific quantity.

senses.def: an additional name of Συμεών 4, the prophet
that which serves to hinder or prevent someone from doing something
a person greeted in Romans 16:15
(an idiom, literally: to burn with intense desire) to have a strong, intense desire for something
glosses: to have a strong lust for
senses.comment: In some languages the equivalent idiom is ‘to boil with desire,’ ‘to feel hot in the genitals,’ or ‘to prefer to die rather than to do.’

senses.def: a person who is in debt
(derivative of ὀφείλω[c] ‘to be under obligation,’ 71.25) one who is obligated to do something

senses.domain: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior
senses.def: (derivative of ὀφείλω[d] ‘to sin against,’ 88.298) one who commits sin and thus incurs a moral debt
(derivative of παραβαίνω[a] ‘to disobey, to break the law,’ 36.28) a person who customarily breaks or disobeys the law
senses.comment: For terms involving ‘disobedience’ or ‘transgression,’ there are often a number of subtle distinctions reflecting several different types of contrasts. For example, there may be important distinctions between disobeying a person and disobeying a law or custom. A number of languages also make a clear distinction between intentional and unintentional disobedience or transgression. Another distinction may involve repeated activity or consistency of attitude, so that the choice of terms may specify whether a person has consistently disobeyed or has only disobeyed once or twice. A further distinction is sometimes made between disobedience of children or those who are mentally incapacitated and the disobedience of those who should know better. Accordingly, in the choice of terms for various passages of Scripture it is extremely important to note the distinctive features of meaning; otherwise, much of the emphasis upon disobedience and transgression as stated in the Scriptures may be seriously distorted.

senses.subdomain: Definite Units of Time: Year, Month, Week, Day, Hour
senses.def: to experience the winter season
glosses: to be in a place during the winter

senses.subdomain: Instruments Used in Binding and Fastening
senses.def: metal chains with special links prepared to go around the ankles; used to restrict the movement of a prisoner
senses.comment: These shackles would normally have consisted of chains with special links prepared to go around the ankles. The equivalent in some languages is simply ‘chains on the feet.’

senses.def: a position or a series of positions around an area, but not necessarily involving complete encirclement
a collective for a group of sheep πρόβατον and/or goats αἴγειος
senses.comment: In instances in which the reference is to a flock of sheep or goats, one can normally employ a designation for any group of animals, though there are often distinct terms for groups of domesticated animals in contrast with groups of wild animals. And in many languages there are a number of different terms for such groupings of animals depending upon the particular animals in question, for example, in English swarm, school, drove, pack, and bevy.

senses.domain: Groups and Classes of Persons and Members of Such Groups and Classes
senses.def: (a figurative extension of meaning of ποίμνη[a] ‘flock,’ 4.28) the followers of Christ constituting a well-defined membership group
glosses: people who are like a flock
senses.comment: It is often impossible to reproduce the figurative values of ἀρνίον[b] (11.29), πρόβατον[b] (11.30), ποίμνιον, and ποίμνη[b], since such metaphors cannot be employed in areas of the world in which sheep serve primarily as scavengers around villages (something which is generally true in many parts of the tropics). It may be possible in some instances to preserve something of the metaphorical value of these four terms by translating in some such manner as ‘take care of my people as you would sheep’ or ‘take care of my people, who are like sheep,’ or ‘take care of my helpless people,’ but frequently one can only translate as ‘take care of my people.’

senses.def: the dwelling of a king or ruler; usually larger and more elaborate than the dwelling of an average person
senses.comment: There are differences of opinion as to the particular πραιτώριον mentioned in Jerusalem. It may have been either the palace of Herod in the western part of the city or the fortress Antonia northwest of the Temple area. The πραιτώριον in Caesarea was the palace built by Herod the Great (see Acts 23:35).|In the Gospels it is satisfactory to translate πραιτώριον[a] as ‘the palace where the governor lived’ or ‘the large dwelling where the ruler lived.’ In a number of languages a term for ‘palace’ often suggests a military fortification, and this would accordingly be quite appropriate for NT usage.

senses.def: a detachment of soldiers serving as the palace guard
to make a decision based upon unjustified preference, with the implication of prejudging
senses.comment: It may be necessary in some languages to define the implications of ‘prejudice’ by saying ‘to decide against someone without any reason’ or ‘to decide against someone without knowing what is true.’

senses.def: to stay or remain in a place beyond some point of time
to continue in an activity or state
senses.comment: It is possible that προσμένω[b] differs from ἐπιμένω[b] in focusing upon the continuity or extent of time involved.

senses.def: a seaport on the coast of Palestine (called Acco in OT times)
a minimal unit of discourse, often a single word
senses.comment: In place of a rendering such as ‘refused to answer a single word’ in Matthew 27:14, it may be more idiomatic to say ‘said nothing’ or ‘refused to speak.’

senses.def: that which has been stated or said, with primary focus upon the content of the communication
senses.comment: Any difference of meaning between λόγος[a] and ῥῆμα[b] would be only a matter of stylistic usage.

senses.def: a happening to which one may refer
the wife of Ἀνανίας 1

senses.subdomain: Cloth, Leather, and Objects Made of Such Materials
senses.def: fabric made of threads from the lustrous tough elastic fiber produced by silkworms for their cocoons; highly valued
pertaining to specialized knowledge resulting in the skill for accomplishing some purpose
senses.comment: In some languages one may render the phrase ‘expert builder’ (1 Corinthians 3:10) as ‘one who knew just how to build best.’

senses.def: pertaining to understanding resulting in wisdom
a person of professional or semi-professional status who is regarded as particularly capable in understanding the philosophical aspects of knowledge and experience
to give off or to reflect a very bright light
to cause to live again together with others
glosses: to raise to life together with
senses.comment: There are serious semantic difficulties involved in a literal translation of συνεγείρω or συζωοποιέω, for a literal rendering could either be interpreted as ‘to be raised to life at the same time with’ or ‘to be raised to life in the same way as,’ but the reference in Colossians 3:1 and Ephesians 2:5 is to a spiritual existence more than to a literal resurrection of the body. This means that both συνεγείρω and συζωοποιέω must be understood as highly figurative. Hence, in Colossians 3:1 it may be necessary to translate εἰ οὖν συνηγέρθητε τῷ Χριστῷ as ‘since you have been raised to life, so to speak, with Christ’ or ‘since, as it were, you have been raised to life with Christ.’ In this way one may point to the fact of a figurative element involved.

senses.def: one who has been arrested and imprisoned along with someone else
senses.comment: A strictly literal rendering of συναιχμάλωτος in the sense of ‘fellow captive’ could be misleading, since it might imply that Paul himself had been a soldier or civilian captured in a war.

senses.def: to cause something to continue along with something else
to exert mental effort in storing information so as to have continual access and use of it
glosses: to cause oneself to be fully aware of
senses.comment: An equivalent of ‘to keep in mind’ may be ‘to keep thinking about’ or ‘to continue to think about’ or even ‘not to stop thinking about.’

senses.domain: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior
senses.def: (derivative of the stem σωφρο ‘to behave in a sensible manner,’ 88.93) pertaining to being sensible and moderate in one’s behavior
senses.comment: In a number of languages terms such as σωφρονισμός[b] (88.93), σωφροσύνη[b] (88.93), σώφρων, and σωφρόνως may be rendered as ‘to have right thoughts about what one should do’ or ‘to let one’s mind guide one’s body.’

senses.def: fourth in a series involving either time, space, or set
a fourth part of an object, series, or mass
senses.comment: For a discussion of some of the translational problems involved, see 60.63.

senses.def: to provide food for, with the implication of a considerable period of time and the food being adequate nourishment
glosses: to give food to someone to eat

senses.def: to take care of, with special reference to supplying necessary nourishment
to raise a child to maturity by providing for physical and psychological needs
senses.comment: To raise or bring up children may be expressed in a number of different ways, for example, ‘to give food to children,’ ‘to take care of children,’ ‘to be a parent to children,’ ‘to cause a child to become an adult,’ or ‘to make a child become like oneself.’

senses.def: pertaining to swelling resulting from the accumulation of lymph in the body tissues
(a technical, nautical term) to brace a ship
the use of magic, often involving drugs and the casting of spells upon people
senses.comment: φαρμακεία and the variant φάρμακον (as in Revelation 9:21) differ from the preceding terms (53.96-53.99) in that the focus is upon the use of certain potions or drugs and the casting of spells.

senses.def: (derivative of φλυαρέω ‘to talk nonsense,’ 33.374) pertaining to talking nonsense

senses.def: to enjoy a state of happiness and well-being

senses.def: dust, soil (see also 2.16)

senses.def: pertaining to being cold, as of objects and masses
